name: Data entry keyers
oneLiner: Fully specified input, verifiable output, no judgement — the pure case of automatable work, and the occupation a German exposure index now ranks first.
threats: The task is the whole job, so nothing has to be redesigned to remove it
Every step is already codified in a system the machine can reach
German exposure scoring puts data entry and text processing first of 140 occupations
Full-time employment of 20- to 24-year-olds in the most exposed occupations fell 14% while the occupations themselves grew

claims.text: Data entry clerks appear on the World Economic Forum's list of fastest-declining job roles to 2030, and employers expect the fall to continue.
The ILO's highest exposure gradient is dominated by clerical roles: data entry clerks, typists, accounting and bookkeeping clerks and general office clerks.
In Microsoft's analysis of real AI usage, the most common and most successful AI-assisted activities are information work — creating, processing and communicating information.

ifo's new indicator ranks data entry and text processing as the most AI-exposed of 140 German occupations, ahead of software development, accounting offices, database and network specialists, and journalists; the share of AI-exposed tasks in the most affected occupations is about five times that in the least affected.

In Germany's most AI-exposed occupations, total employment rose 1.8% since the third quarter of 2022 and employment in the least exposed occupations fell 6.4%, while full-time employment of 20- to 24-year-olds in the most exposed occupations fell 14%, from about 279,000 to 239,000.

IAB's separate study of about 22.3 million German full-time employees finds full-time employment of 20- to 29-year-olds in highly exposed occupations 3.8% below its 2022 level, against 2.6% in less exposed ones — a 1.2 percentage point gap that is not statistically significant for the age group overall and is smaller than the effect of the downturn.

Both teams measure the share of an occupation's tasks an AI system could do, not whether employers have adopted it, and neither attributes the age pattern to AI alone; ifo names demographic change, longer training periods and harder onboarding under remote work as untested alternatives.
